trust_decision.summary: nghttpx decides where a client request message ends and opaque tunnel bytes begin for CONNECT / HTTP Upgrade requests: the HTTP/1 frontend lets an upgrade request carry Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding body bytes and, once the backend says upgraded, forwards the raw read buffer, while the HTTP/1 backend connection flushes buffered body before the 101/2xx is seen, so front end and back end can disagree on message boundaries.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'Upgrade request with Content-Length'; the HTTP/1 frontend's request header callback is where inspect_http1_request() marks upgrade_request and Content-Length/TE are handled.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP/1.1 frontend: CONNECT or Upgrade request headers with Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding (reject)
HTTP/1.1 frontend: body bytes delivered by llhttp for an upgrade/CONNECT request (reject)
HTTP/1.1 frontend: request message completion sets new http1_msg_complete flag
HTTP/1.1 frontend: raw tunnel forwarding after upgrade now gated on request message completion
HTTP/1.1 frontend: error logging for HPE_USER
HTTP/2 frontend: CONNECT (incl. extended CONNECT :protocol websocket) HEADERS with content-length (reject 400)
HTTP/3 frontend: CONNECT HEADERS with content-length (reject 400)
HTTP/1 backend connection: request body chunks for any frontend held in blocked buffer until upgrade is confirmed
HTTP/1 backend connection: end of request body for upgrade request held
HTTP/1 backend response: CONNECT 2xx without upgrade fulfilled mapped to 502
HTTP/1 backend response: chunked flag ignored when upgraded; non-101 response to upgrade request forces connection close; blocked body flushed on 101
HTTP/1 backend first write: blocked body no longer flushed with headers for upgrade requests
Backend connection pooling: do not reuse connection while blocked request buffer still holds bytes

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report names an HTTP/1 'Upgrade request'; HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 have no Upgrade header and use DATA framing, and libnghttp2 already validates content-length, so a solver can argue the h2/h3 frontends cannot smuggle; the backend writer can be dismissed as 'the frontend now rejects the body, so nothing reaches it'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate tunnels must keep working: CONNECT and WebSocket upgrades (h1 Upgrade and h2/h3 extended CONNECT translated to GET+Upgrade) whose client sends tunnel bytes right after the headers must have those bytes forwarded once the 101/2xx arrives; ordinary keep-alive POSTs with Content-Length or chunked bodies, and backend connection reuse, must be unaffected. An over-broad fix (reject any bytes after upgrade headers, or drop the blocked buffer) breaks these.
